Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the written anti-fraud plan and SIU procedure set for all 51 jurisdictions; escalates drafting disputes to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and legal questions to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act (Model 680) sections on the anti-fraud plan and SIU, re-read against each adopting state's own text at each annual review; representative Alaska Division of Insurance anti-fraud plan / SIU requirement, with Arizona, California (Ins. Code 1875.20-1875.24 and 10 CCR 2698.30-2698.43) and Connecticut anti-fraud plan / SIU requirements as supporting cites, plus NY 11 NYCRR 86 (Reg 95) and Fla. Stat. 626.9891 for the plan-filing states

In-scope processes.value: Claim intake and adjudication referral to SIU, underwriting and premium-fraud detection, producer and internal fraud, SIU investigation and case closure, mandatory reporting to state fraud bureaus, and anti-fraud training - across all lines and all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: FRISS scoring and referral rules plus the SIU case record in Guidewire ClaimCenter; the approved plan PDF and the per-state requirement matrix live in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Anti-Fraud Plan and SIU Procedure Manual - SIU charter and staffing, red-flag referral triggers by line, investigation standards, state-by-state mandatory reporting matrix (bureau, form, day count), immunity and confidentiality handling, training curriculum, and TPA/vendor obligations

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel legal clearance; full review every 12 months and an out-of-cycle amendment within 30 days of any state statute, regulation or bulletin change (NY 11 NYCRR 86 requires plan amendments be filed within 30 days)

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual plan review closes before the earliest state filing date; plan/report filings tracked per state - Florida anti-fraud plan and SIU report by December 31 (Fla. Stat. 626.9891), New York Reg 95 annual SIU report by March 15, California SIU annual compliance report to the CDI Fraud Division, plus 30-day amendment filings on any material plan change

Deadline reminders configured.value: Annual review kickoff reminder at T-120 days from the December 31 Florida filing date, plus per-state filing reminders at T-60/T-30/T-7 and a 30-day amendment timer opened automatically when a state legislative-tracking alert is accepted

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved plan version, its redline, the legal clearance memo, per-state filing receipts and the training completion extract retained 7 years from the date the version is superseded, indexed by jurisdiction and plan version

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A jurisdiction operating without a current approved plan section, an unfiled amendment past 30 days, or a procedure step contradicted by actual SIU practice is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the annual plan approval and every remediation closing a plan-content or plan-filing exception; SIU Manager may not self-approve

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 51 jurisdictions crossed with the required plan elements (SIU existence and staffing, referral triggers, reporting route, training, record retention), plus every plan amendment made in the last 12 months

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on two conditions - a jurisdiction with no current plan section covering a mandated element, and any amendment filed after its state deadline; on the remaining documentation attributes an exception rate above 5 percent of tested attributes fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review with event-driven amendments; the test runs annually within 60 days of plan approval, with an interim amendment test each quarter over amendments raised that quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the SIU and must not have drafted or edited any plan section under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual anti-fraud plan test workpaper (requirement matrix extract, sampled state re-performance, filing receipts, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Anti-Fraud Plan / plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved plan PDF, SIU org chart and investigator credentials, per-state filing receipts, training completion report and the referral-procedure extract, producible for a market conduct exam data request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance is the single point of contact for fraud-bureau and DOI inquiries on the plan; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a missing or late plan element before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Pull the current approved plan and its per-state filing footprint
actions: Open the compliance evidence repository under Anti-Fraud Plan and download the latest approved plan PDF, its redline and the approval memo signed by the Head of Compliance.
Export the per-state filing register (jurisdiction, filing required Y/N, statutory cite, portal, last filed date, next due date) into the annual review workbook.
Ask the SIU Manager for the current SIU org chart, headcount by state, and investigator licences or certifications so the staffing section can be refreshed.
Open a plan review folder named anti-fraud-plan-<review year> and drop all three artefacts into it.
checklist.done: the review folder holds the current approved plan, its redline, the approval memo and a filing register covering all 51 jurisdictions.

checklist.step: Refresh the 51-jurisdiction anti-fraud requirement matrix
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open the regulatory change feed and filter Category = Market Conduct, Topic = Insurance Fraud, effective dates in the last 12 months.

For each of the 51 jurisdictions record on the matrix: statutory cite, whether a written anti-fraud plan is mandated, whether the plan must be filed with the department, whether an SIU is mandated or may be outsourced, the fraud bureau that receives reports, the mandatory reporting form and the reporting day count.
Re-read the representative Alaska anti-fraud plan / SIU requirement and the Arizona, California and Connecticut requirements in full, and flag any element the current plan does not address.
Note every state that requires an annual SIU report separately from the plan (New York Reg 95, Florida, California) with its due date.
Sign and date the matrix and hand it to the SIU Manager as the drafting brief.
checklist.done: each of the 51 jurisdictions has a dated matrix row with cite, plan-filing flag, SIU mandate, bureau, form and day count, signed by counsel.

checklist.step: Rewrite the SIU charter and staffing section against the refreshed matrix
actions: Update the charter to state SIU reporting line, independence from claims settlement authority, headcount, geographic coverage and the investigator-to-claim-volume ratio.
List the states that set a minimum SIU staffing or in-state investigator requirement and show how the current establishment meets it.
Record which investigative activities are outsourced (surveillance, EUO counsel, forensic accounting) and name the vendor and contract reference for each.
Attach current investigator credentials - state private-investigator licences, CFE or FCLS designations - as an appendix schedule.
checklist.done: the charter states reporting line, independence, headcount, per-state staffing coverage and an appendix of investigator credentials.

checklist.step: Document the claims red-flag and referral procedure line by line
actions: For each line of business (auto, property, liability, life, disability, workers compensation) list the mandatory red-flag indicators an adjuster must act on, drawn from the NAIC fraud indicator set and the company loss experience.

Write the referral mechanics against the actual screens: in Guidewire ClaimCenter open the claim, use Actions then New Special Investigation, complete the Referral Reason, Indicators Observed and Narrative fields, and attach the supporting documents.
State the service standard - adjuster refers within 2 business days of observing an indicator, SIU acknowledges within 3 business days and dispositions within 30 days.
State explicitly that a claim referred to SIU is not denied on suspicion alone and that claim-handling deadlines under each state prompt-pay rule continue to run.
Have the Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager confirm the drafted screen path matches the deployed ClaimCenter configuration.
checklist.done: the procedure names the indicators per line, the exact ClaimCenter referral path and the acknowledge/disposition service standards, confirmed against the live configuration.

checklist.step: Document the underwriting, premium and producer fraud procedures
actions: Write the application-fraud section: rate evasion and garaging misrepresentation checks, identity and prior-loss verification, and the point in new business where a suspect application is routed to SIU.
Write the premium-fraud section for commercial lines: payroll and class-code misstatement found on premium audit, and the handoff from the Premium Auditor to SIU.

Write the producer-fraud section: premium diversion, fictitious policies and unauthorised binding, with the route to the Producer Compliance Manager and to the state department that licenses the producer.
State that any internal-employee suspicion routes to the Financial Crime Investigator and the Ethics Officer rather than through the normal claims referral queue.
Record where each suspect case is opened in the policy administration platform and how it is cross-linked to the SIU case number.
checklist.done: application, premium, producer and internal fraud each have a written detection trigger, routing owner and case-linking rule.

checklist.step: Build the mandatory reporting matrix into the procedure
actions: Convert counsel's matrix into an operational table: state, bureau (for example the Alaska Division of Insurance fraud unit, the New York DFS Insurance Frauds Bureau, the California DOI Fraud Division), submission route (NAIC Online Fraud Reporting System, state portal, or state form), form name and the day count from determination of suspicion.
Record the specific forms where they exist - California eFD-1 within 60 days of determination, New York FFA-1 within 30 days - and the default NAIC OFRS route for states without a bespoke form.
Add the NICB questionable-claim referral step and state that a NICB referral does not satisfy a statutory bureau report.
State who submits (SIU Investigator) and who evidences the submission (SIU Manager files the confirmation number on the case record).
Have Regulatory Counsel initial the day counts before the table is published.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a bureau, route, form and day count in the procedure, initialled by counsel.

checklist.step: Write the immunity, confidentiality and privacy handling section
actions: State the statutory immunity that attaches to good-faith fraud reporting in each adopting state and the conditions that preserve it.
State that SIU case files are confidential, are not released to the insured or a third party without legal process, and name the counsel who clears any subpoena response.
Set the rule for handling medical, genetic and financial data inside SIU files, including minimum-necessary access and the retention clock.
Prohibit the use of a fraud referral as the sole basis for an adverse underwriting decision without an independent factual finding, and record the reference to each state unfair claims practices act.
checklist.done: immunity, confidentiality, sensitive-data handling and the adverse-action prohibition are each written with a statutory reference.

checklist.step: Specify the anti-fraud training curriculum and audience
actions: Define three curricula in Cornerstone LMS: all-staff fraud awareness (annual), claims and underwriting red-flag training (annual, role-assigned), and SIU investigator continuing education (annual hours).
Assign each curriculum to the correct job-code audience so new hires are auto-enrolled within 30 days of start date.
Set the completion deadline and the escalation to the line manager at 14 days overdue.
Record in the plan that the LMS completion extract is the evidence of training and name the report used to produce it.
checklist.done: three curricula exist in the LMS with job-code assignment rules, deadlines and a named completion report cited in the plan.

checklist.step: Bind TPAs, MGAs and outsourced adjusters to the plan
actions: List every third party that handles claims or underwriting on the company paper and pull its contract from the contract lifecycle management repository.
Confirm each contract carries the anti-fraud clause: referral obligation to the company SIU, cooperation with state fraud bureaus, record retention and audit rights.
Where the clause is missing, raise a contract amendment with the Contracts Manager and put the vendor on the exception log until it is executed.
Collect each TPA current anti-fraud procedure and attach it as a plan appendix.
checklist.done: every claims-handling third party is either clause-compliant with its procedure attached or sitting on the exception log with an amendment in flight.

checklist.step: Align the plan text to the deployed detection and case configuration
actions: In FRISS open the rule and model configuration and export the active detection rules, score thresholds and auto-referral triggers.
Compare each documented red flag in the plan to a live FRISS rule or an explicit manual-only indicator, and close every gap in one direction or the other.
Confirm the FRISS score threshold that raises an automatic referral matches the number printed in the procedure.
Record the mandatory SIU case fields (referral source, indicators, investigation steps, disposition code, bureau report reference) and confirm they are required fields in the case record.
checklist.done: every plan red flag maps to a live FRISS rule or a stated manual indicator, and the documented score threshold equals the deployed threshold.

checklist.step: Run the annual review workshop and produce the redline
actions: Convene SIU, Claims, Underwriting, Legal, Learning and Vendor Management for the annual review and work the matrix gap list line by line.
Bring last year exam findings, complaint themes and internal audit issues into the session and confirm each has been reflected in the plan text.
Produce a redline against the prior approved version with a change register recording section, change, driver (statute change, exam finding, process change) and author.
Set the disposition of every gap: text change, system change, or accepted with rationale - no gap leaves the session undecided.
checklist.done: a redline and a change register exist, and every matrix gap has a recorded disposition.

checklist.step: Obtain legal clearance and Head of Compliance approval
actions: Route the redline to Regulatory Counsel, who confirms in writing that each state mandated element is addressed and that the reporting day counts are correct.
Review the change register and the accepted-gap rationales, and reject any acceptance that leaves a mandated element uncovered.
Sign and date the approval memo naming the plan version number and the effective date.
Instruct that the approved version be locked as read-only in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated approval memo names the plan version, backed by a written counsel clearance, and the version is locked.

checklist.step: File the plan and amendments with the states that require it
actions: Work the filing register state by state: submit through the NAIC Antifraud Plan Repository where the state accepts it, and through the state portal where it does not (Florida DFS by December 31, New York DFS Insurance Frauds Bureau, California DOI Fraud Division).
For each submission capture the confirmation number, submission date and the receiving unit, and attach the submitted PDF exactly as filed.
Where the change is an amendment to a previously filed plan, file within the state amendment window - 30 days under New York 11 NYCRR 86 - and record the trigger date the clock ran from.
Update the filing register next-due dates and load the reminders at T-60/T-30/T-7.
Escalate any state portal rejection to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager the same business day.
checklist.done: every filing-required jurisdiction shows a confirmation number, the filed PDF and a refreshed next-due date.

checklist.step: Publish the plan, attest and train the population
actions: Publish the approved version to the compliance intranet page and retire the prior version so only one plan is reachable.
Launch the annual fraud-awareness and red-flag curricula in Cornerstone LMS with a 45-day completion window.
Require claims, underwriting and SIU staff to attest that they have read the version and understood the referral obligation.
Pull the completion and attestation report at day 45 and escalate outstanding staff to their line manager and the divisional head.
checklist.done: the current version is the only published version, and the completion and attestation report shows a documented chase for every outstanding individual.

checklist.step: File and index the plan evidence for retention
actions: Move the plan version, redline, change register, counsel clearance, approval memo, state filing confirmations and LMS completion extract into the compliance evidence repository under Anti-Fraud Plan / <plan year>.
Apply the retention label of 7 years from supersession so the version survives a later plan rewrite.
Index the record so it is retrievable by jurisdiction, plan version and filing confirmation number.
Confirm read access for Market Conduct Compliance and Internal Audit and restrict edit access to the SIU Manager and Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the full plan evidence set is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by jurisdiction and version.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdictions and mandated plan elements
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every anti-fraud plan and SIU obligation in force for the 51 jurisdictions the company is licensed in.
Cross each jurisdiction with the mandated elements (written plan, SIU, referral triggers, bureau reporting route and day count, training, retention) to form the attribute population.
Confirm the licensed-jurisdiction list agrees to the certificate-of-authority register held by the Regulatory Affairs Manager and resolve any difference before testing.
Record the population size and extraction date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the attribute population is built, reconciled to the certificate-of-authority register and dated.

testing.step: Reconcile the filing register to the actual state submissions
actions: Match every jurisdiction flagged filing-required on the register to a submission confirmation number and a filed PDF.
Compare the filed PDF version number to the approved plan version in the repository - a filed version that is not the approved version is an exception.
List any filing-required jurisdiction with no confirmation, and any amendment filed later than its state window, as automatic exceptions.
Reconcile the register jurisdiction count back to the population count and explain any difference.
testing.done: every filing-required jurisdiction is matched to a confirmed submission of the approved version or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the state sample
actions: Take 100 percent of the plan-filing states (including Florida, New York and California) and 100 percent of states that changed statute in the review year.
Take 12 further jurisdictions at random using a seeded, reproducible selection from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and the resulting state list in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note the representative Alaska requirement as a mandatory in-sample state given it drives the plan text.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every plan-filing and statute-changed jurisdiction plus Alaska.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement read for each sampled state
actions: Open the current statutory and regulatory text for the sampled state in the Internal Regulatory System and read it before looking at the requirement matrix.
Write your own conclusion on plan mandated, plan filing required, SIU mandated, bureau, form and day count.
Compare to the matrix row - a right answer with a wrong or stale citation is still an exception.
Capture the source text page into the workpaper with the date it was read.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent conclusion, a comparison to the matrix and a dated source capture.

testing.step: Trace each sampled requirement into the plan text
actions: For each sampled state, locate the plan section and paragraph that satisfies each mandated element and record the section reference on the attribute sheet.
Reject a generic statement such as the company complies with applicable law as satisfying a specific mandated element.
Confirm the state appears in the operational reporting matrix with its bureau, form and day count, not only in the narrative.
Flag any element supported only by an appendix that is not part of the approved and filed version.
testing.done: every mandated element for every sampled state traces to a named, approved plan section or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Test that the documented procedure matches operating practice
actions: Select 25 SIU cases opened in the last 12 months across at least 5 states and open each in Guidewire ClaimCenter.
Confirm the referral was raised through the path the procedure describes, with the Referral Reason and Indicators Observed fields completed.
Measure the elapsed days from indicator date to referral, and from referral to SIU acknowledgement, against the 2 and 3 business day standards.
Where the procedure describes a step the case record has no field for, record it as a plan-versus-practice exception against the SIU Manager.
testing.done: the sampled cases either follow the documented path within the stated service standards or the divergence is logged as a plan-versus-practice exception.

testing.step: Verify the detection configuration equals the documented thresholds
actions: Export the active FRISS rule set, model version and auto-referral score threshold as at the test date.
Compare the exported threshold and rule list to the numbers and indicators printed in the approved plan.
Check the change history for any threshold change made since plan approval without a corresponding plan amendment.
Record the exported configuration as workpaper evidence with its extraction timestamp.
testing.done: deployed rules and thresholds reconcile to the approved plan, or every unreconciled change is logged with its change date.

testing.step: Recompute the amendment and filing deadline maths
actions: For each plan amendment in the year, identify the trigger date (statute effective date, exam finding date or process go-live) from source evidence rather than the register.
Recompute the due date as trigger date plus the state amendment window - 30 days for New York 11 NYCRR 86 - and compare to the actual submission date.
Recompute the annual filing dates against the state deadlines, including the Florida December 31 date and the New York March 15 annual SIU report.
Any submission after the recomputed date is a reportable breach and not merely a test exception.
testing.done: every amendment and annual filing has a recomputed due date and a documented on-time or late conclusion.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception recording jurisdiction, missing element, source evidence and regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (statutory change not tracked, drafting omission, configuration drift, vendor clause missing, filing missed) and name an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a missing filing or a late amendment, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel before any contact with the state.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the plan test
actions: Compute the attribute exception rate and compare it to the 5 percent threshold and the two zero-tolerance conditions.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted no part of the plan, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any zero-tolerance breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions and the MCAS blank for each participating line for the reporting data year, re-read at each filing season, alongside the state MCAS participation bulletins; substantive fraud obligations sit under the Alaska anti-fraud plan / SIU requirement with Arizona, California and Connecticut supporting cites

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Data year ends December 31; MCAS submissions for property/casualty, life, annuity, long-term care, disability income and lender-placed lines are due April 30, and the health lines on the later NAIC deadline of June 30; state MCAS registration must be completed before the submission window opens

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar milestones at T-90 (data extract freeze), T-60 (validation complete), T-30 (attestation pack to the signing officer) and T-7 (submission confirmed) against each of the April 30 and June 30 deadlines, per state and line

Evidence location for test results.value: MCAS test workpaper (participation determination, source-to-blank reconciliation, sampled element re-performance, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under MCAS / <data year>

checklist.step: Determine the state and line participation set for the data year
actions: Pull direct written premium by state, by line and by writing company for the data year ending December 31 from the statutory reporting ledger.
Compare each state and line to the MCAS participation threshold published in the NAIC Data Call and Definitions and mark in-scope or out-of-scope.
Check the current NAIC list of MCAS participating states and the lines each has adopted, since not every state takes every line.

Produce the participation grid (state, line, writing company, premium, in-scope Y/N, threshold applied) and have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the premium figures agree to the Annual Statement state page.
checklist.done: a participation grid exists for every state and line with the premium figure, the threshold applied and a confirmation that premium ties to the state page.

checklist.step: Register and confirm iSite+ access for every in-scope state
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company credentials and open the Market Conduct Annual Statement application.
For each writing company (by NAIC company code) and each in-scope state and line, confirm the registration is active for the data year and add any missing registration.
Verify the named contact, filing key and attesting officer details on file are current, and correct any leaver still listed.
Screenshot the registration confirmation screen per company and file it in the MCAS data-year folder.
checklist.done: every in-scope company/state/line is registered for the data year with a current contact and a captured confirmation screen.

checklist.step: Read the current Data Call and Definitions and record the changes
actions: Download the NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions and the blank for each participating line for this data year.
Diff it against last year version and list every added, removed or redefined element, including changed claim-count definitions and new interrogatories.
For each change, name the source system field affected and the owner who must revise the extract.
Circulate the change list to Claims, Policy Administration, Complaints and SIU with a response date before the T-90 extract freeze.
checklist.done: a dated change list names every definition change, the affected source field and an owner with a response date.

checklist.step: Refresh the data dictionary that maps source fields to MCAS elements
actions: Open the MCAS mapping document and confirm every element on the blank has a source table, column, filter and transformation rule.
Apply the change list from the Data Call diff and update the affected mappings, recording the version and the author on each changed row.
Confirm the state-allocation rule for each element (risk state versus policy-issue state) matches the NAIC definition for that line.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager review and sign the mapping before it is used to build the extract.
checklist.done: every MCAS element has a signed source-to-target mapping, including the state-allocation rule.

checklist.step: Build and freeze the data-year extract
actions: Run the MCAS extract job against the frozen data-year snapshot so later transactional activity cannot move the numbers.
Produce the element-level output by state, line and writing company, plus a record-count log per source feed.
Record the extract run id, snapshot date and row counts in the run log and lock the output tables read-only.
Hand the extract and the run log to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst at the T-90 freeze milestone.
checklist.done: a locked, timestamped extract with a per-feed record-count log is delivered at the T-90 freeze.

checklist.step: Reconcile the extract to the source systems and the Annual Statement
actions: Reconcile MCAS direct written premium by state to the Annual Statement state page and explain every difference in writing.
Reconcile claim counts opened, closed with payment and closed without payment to the Guidewire ClaimCenter operational report for the same period.
Reconcile complaint counts to the complaints register and to the NAIC complaint records the Consumer Affairs Manager holds.
Reconcile policy counts in force at year end to the Policy Administration Platform inventory report.
Log each reconciling item with an amount, a cause and a sign-off, and clear anything unexplained before validation.
checklist.done: premium, claim, complaint and policy counts each reconcile to their source of record with every difference explained and signed.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC validation and reasonability checks
actions: Upload the draft file into the iSite+ MCAS application and run the built-in validations before final submission.
Work every hard error to zero and document a written explanation for every soft warning that remains.
Run the internal reasonability suite: year-on-year movement over 20 percent by element, claim closure ratios, denial ratios and suit counts per 1,000 claims.
Send any element that fails reasonability back to the owning function for a written cause before it is filed.
checklist.done: zero hard errors remain and every soft warning and reasonability break has a documented written explanation.

checklist.step: Draft and evidence the MCAS interrogatory answers
actions: Work through the interrogatory section of each line blank and draft an answer supported by a named internal artefact rather than a recollection.
For questions touching claim-handling practice, take the answer from the current claims procedure and cite its version.
Where the answer would differ by state, confirm whether the blank permits a state-level answer before generalising.
Attach the supporting artefact reference to each answer in the working file so the answer is defensible in an exam.
checklist.done: every interrogatory has a drafted answer with a cited supporting artefact and version.

checklist.step: Assemble the attestation pack for the signing officer
actions: Build the pack: participation grid, final element file per state and line, reconciliation summary, validation log with soft-warning explanations and the interrogatory answers.
Include a one-page summary of the largest year-on-year movements with their causes so the officer is not attesting blind.
Deliver the pack to the attesting officer at the T-30 milestone with the deadline date stated on the cover.
Record the officer questions and the answers given in the pack file.
checklist.done: the signing officer holds a complete pack at T-30 including movement explanations and a documented question log.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Review the attestation pack and challenge any element whose movement has no substantiated cause.
Confirm the participation grid covers every state where premium exceeded the threshold before signing.
Sign the MCAS attestation for each writing company and data year and date it.
Return the signed attestation to Regulatory Reporting for upload and filing.
checklist.done: a dated attestation is signed for each writing company with no unexplained element outstanding.

checklist.step: Submit each state and line file in iSite+
actions: In the iSite+ MCAS application select the data year, company and line, upload the validated file and complete the attestation step.
Submit each state file before the April 30 deadline, and the health lines before the June 30 deadline, working the highest-premium states first.
Capture the submission confirmation number, timestamp and status for every state and line into the filing register.
Re-open the application 24 hours after submission and confirm the status shows as accepted rather than pending or rejected.
checklist.done: every in-scope state and line shows an accepted submission with a captured confirmation number ahead of its deadline.

checklist.step: Clear rejections and post-submission NAIC queries
actions: Monitor the iSite+ message centre and the MCAS contact mailbox daily through the filing season.
Triage each query into data error, definition difference or genuine business result, and involve the source-system owner where the data is wrong.
Where a correction is needed, obtain the Head of Compliance sign-off, refile the corrected file and record the restatement in the filing register.
Answer each query in writing within 5 business days and file the exchange with the submission evidence.
checklist.done: no query is older than 5 business days and every correction is signed off, refiled and recorded as a restatement.

checklist.step: Report the filed results into market conduct monitoring
actions: Load the filed MCAS elements into the market conduct dashboard alongside the prior three data years.

Compute the ratios that regulators build from MCAS - claim denial rate, closed-without-payment rate, median settlement days, complaint rate per 1,000 policies - and compare to the industry position where NAIC scorecards are available.
Flag any ratio that would place the company in an outlier band and open a monitoring item under the quarterly conduct-metric process.
Brief Claims and Underwriting leadership on the outliers before a regulator raises them.
checklist.done: the filed data is loaded, the regulator-facing ratios are computed and every outlier band has an opened monitoring item.

checklist.step: Run the post-season lessons-learned and update the procedure
actions: Convene Claims, Policy Administration, Complaints, SIU and Data Engineering within 30 days of the last submission.
Review every reconciling item, validation error, restatement and late milestone from the season and assign a cause.
Update the MCAS Filing Procedure and the data dictionary for each agreed fix, with an owner and a date ahead of the next T-90 freeze.
Record the actions in the filing register so next season opens with them visible.
checklist.done: every reconciling item, error and restatement has an assigned cause and a dated procedure or mapping fix.

checklist.step: File and retain the MCAS evidence set
actions: File the submitted files, confirmations, reconciliations, validation logs, interrogatory support and signed attestations under MCAS / <data year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the submission date.
Index by data year, state, line and writing company so an exam request can be met without a rebuild.
Confirm the frozen extract snapshot is retained alongside the submission so the numbers can be re-derived.
checklist.done: the MCAS evidence set including the frozen extract is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and indexed by state and line.

testing.step: Rebuild the participation population independently
actions: Take direct written premium by state, line and writing company for the data year straight from the Annual Statement state pages rather than from the participation grid.
Apply the NAIC MCAS participation threshold yourself and derive your own in-scope list.
Compare your list to the filed participation grid and treat every state or line you have and the company does not as a potential missed filing.
Record the population size, source and derivation date in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently derived participation list exists and every difference to the filed grid is listed for investigation.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted data back to the source of record
actions: Select premium, claims opened, claims closed without payment, complaints and policies in force for 8 states and re-extract them from the frozen snapshot.
Compare your re-extraction to the submitted file element by element and compute the variance.
Apply the tolerance - exact on premium, 0.5 percent on counts - and log every break above it.
Confirm the frozen snapshot is genuinely immutable by re-running one prior extract and matching the row counts.
testing.done: sampled elements for 8 states reconcile within tolerance to a re-extraction from an immutable snapshot, or the break is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the element sample
actions: Take 100 percent of states whose submission was restated or filed after the deadline.
Take 10 further state/line combinations at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, weighted toward the highest-premium states.
Within each selection, sample 15 MCAS elements including at least one claim-count, one timeliness and one complaint element.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all restated or late states and includes claim-count, timeliness and complaint elements.

testing.step: Re-perform the definition application on sampled elements
actions: Read the NAIC Data Call and Definitions entry for each sampled element before opening the mapping document.
Write your own filter and transformation logic, then compare it to the signed data dictionary row.
Test the state-allocation rule specifically - a risk-state element allocated on policy-issue state is an exception even where the total is right.
Capture the definition text and the mapping row side by side in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled element has an independent definition read, a mapping comparison and a captured evidence pair.

testing.step: Trace each sampled submission to its iSite+ confirmation
actions: In the iSite+ MCAS application open the filing history for the sampled company, state, line and data year.
Confirm the confirmation number in the filing register matches the application record and that the status reads accepted.
Compare the file version accepted by NAIC to the file version attached to the signed attestation - a mismatch is an exception.
Capture the filing history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled submission traces to an accepted iSite+ record whose file version matches the attested file.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths for every submission
actions: List each submission timestamp by state, line and data year from the iSite+ record rather than the internal register.
Compare each to its statutory deadline - April 30 for the property/casualty, life, annuity, long-term care, disability income and lender-placed lines, June 30 for the health lines.
Compute the days early or late per submission and identify any that landed inside the final 48 hours as a process risk even where on time.
Treat any submission after its deadline as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every submission has a recomputed days-early or days-late figure against the correct deadline.

testing.step: Test the interrogatory answers against operating reality
actions: Select 10 interrogatory answers, weighted to those describing claim-handling and fraud-referral practice.
Open the cited supporting artefact at the version cited and confirm it actually says what the answer asserts.
For two answers, test the practice directly against a small claim sample rather than relying on the document.
Log any answer that is accurate on paper but contradicted in practice as an exception with the claim numbers that show it.
testing.done: each sampled interrogatory answer is supported by the cited artefact and two are corroborated against actual claim handling.

testing.step: Verify the attestation and segregation of duties
actions: Confirm a signed, dated attestation exists for every writing company and that the signature pre-dates the submission timestamp.
Confirm the attesting officer is not the person who prepared or uploaded the file.
Check the iSite+ user account that performed each upload against the joiners and leavers list for the season.
Log any submission uploaded by an account belonging to a leaver or a shared account as a control exception.
testing.done: every submission has a pre-dated attestation from an officer independent of the preparer, uploaded from an identified active account.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with data year, state, line, element and the size of the misstatement.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (definition misread, mapping stale, source data quality, missed participation, late milestone) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a filed element was materially wrong, open a restatement decision with the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next season pre-submission dry run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the MCAS test
actions: Compute the element exception rate and compare it to the tolerance and the two zero-tolerance conditions of a missed state and a late filing.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and attested nothing in the submission, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under MCAS / <data year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

In-scope systems.value: Market conduct dashboard in Power BI built over the enterprise data warehouse, fed by Guidewire ClaimCenter claim and SIU case data, FRISS referral scores and the complaints register

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metric Monitoring Procedure - metric definitions and formulas, source feeds, benchmark sources, threshold and trigger bands, escalation routes and the quarterly review agenda

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance annually and re-approved whenever a metric definition, threshold band or benchmark source changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle - data cut at quarter end, pack produced within 20 business days, conduct committee review by day 30, and any red-band item raised into the issue tracker within 5 business days of the review

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar milestones at quarter end plus 5 (feeds delivered), plus 12 (metrics computed and validated), plus 20 (pack issued) and plus 30 (committee reviewed), each with an owner named on the reminder

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any metric breaching its red band, any state where SIU referrals fell to zero for a quarter, and any missed pack deadline is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the closure of every red-band metric item and any decision to reset a threshold band

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All metrics in the quarterly pack for the quarter under test, crossed with the 51 jurisdictions, plus every red and amber band item raised in the last four quarters

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Recomputed metrics must match the published pack exactly on counts and within 0.1 percentage points on ratios; any red-band item without a raised issue within 5 business days is a fail, as is any quarter published after day 20

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Quarterly pack, metric definition sheet, per-state metric tables and the red-band remediation log, producible for a market analysis inquiry or exam interrogatory within 5 business days

checklist.step: Confirm the metric definitions and threshold bands for the quarter
actions: Open the metric definition sheet and confirm each metric carries a formula, numerator and denominator source, state-allocation rule and threshold bands (green, amber, red).

Confirm the fraud metrics are present - SIU referral rate per 1,000 claims, SIU acceptance rate, average days from referral to disposition, bureau reports filed within the statutory day count, and recovery or savings recorded.
Confirm the conduct metrics regulators build from MCAS are present - denial rate, closed-without-payment rate, median settlement days and complaint rate per 1,000 policies.
Record any definition change agreed since last quarter with its approval reference so the trend line is annotated rather than silently broken.
checklist.done: every metric has a formula, sources, state rule and bands, and every change since last quarter is annotated with its approval.

checklist.step: Collect the SIU case feed for the quarter
actions: Export from the SIU case module every case opened, closed and still open in the quarter with state, line, referral source, referral date, acceptance date, disposition code and disposition date.
Include the bureau report reference and submission date on every case where a report was required.
Confirm no case is missing a disposition code and chase the owning investigator on any that are before the feed is released.
Sign the feed as complete and hand it to the Data Analyst with the row count.
checklist.done: the SIU feed is complete with disposition codes on every case, carries bureau report references, and is signed with a row count.

checklist.step: Collect the claims, complaints and underwriting feeds
actions: Pull claims opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, denied and reopened by state and line for the quarter from the claims mart.
Pull complaints from the complaints register split by DOI-received and direct-to-company, with received date, state and root-cause code, from the Consumer Affairs Manager feed.
Pull underwriting and premium-fraud case counts from the policy administration platform and producer-fraud cases from the Producer Compliance Manager.
Reconcile each feed row count to the source system operational report and record the reconciliation in the run log.
checklist.done: all four feeds are loaded with row counts reconciled to their source operational reports.

checklist.step: Compute the metrics by state and validate the maths
actions: Refresh the market conduct dataset and compute every metric at company, state and line grain for the quarter and the trailing eight quarters.
Apply the small-population rule so a state with fewer than 30 claims in the quarter is shown as not meaningful rather than as a wild ratio.
Run the validation suite: numerators never exceed denominators, state totals sum to the company total, and trailing-quarter values are unchanged from last quarter published pack.
Log any restated prior-quarter value with its cause on the restatement tab.
checklist.done: metrics compute at all three grains, pass the validation suite, and every restated prior value is explained.

checklist.step: Refresh the external benchmarks
actions: Capture the current NAIC complaint index for the company by line from the NAIC Consumer Information Source and record the capture date.
Where NAIC MCAS scorecard or industry aggregate ratios are available for the line, capture the industry median and quartile positions.
Record the peer group used and why, so a later reader can see the comparison is like for like.
File the benchmark captures as dated PDFs alongside the pack so the comparison can be reproduced.
checklist.done: each benchmarked metric has a dated external capture, a named peer group and a filed source PDF.

checklist.step: Band every metric and identify the outliers
actions: Apply the green, amber and red bands to every metric at company and state grain.
Add the trend trigger: three consecutive quarters moving adversely puts a metric into amber even where the level is still green.

Flag structural outliers explicitly - any state with zero SIU referrals for the quarter, any state where bureau reports filed on time falls below 100 percent, and any state whose complaint index exceeds 1.00.
Produce the outlier list with the state, metric, value, band and prior-quarter value.
checklist.done: every metric is banded at company and state grain and the outlier list names each breach with its prior-quarter value.

checklist.step: Investigate each outlier to a stated cause
actions: For each outlier, drill from the dashboard to the underlying claim, case or complaint list and read at least 5 records.
Classify the cause: genuine conduct issue, one large event (a catastrophe or a single fraud ring), data quality defect, or definitional artefact.
For zero-referral states, check whether the FRISS rules are actually firing in that state or the state was excluded from a rule deployment.
Write the cause and the evidence reference onto the outlier row - no outlier is carried forward with an unexplained cause.
checklist.done: every outlier carries a classified cause backed by named records or a configuration finding.

checklist.step: Test the bureau-reporting timeliness metric case by case
actions: List every case in the quarter where a determination of suspected fraud was recorded and a state report was therefore required.

For each, compute days from the determination date to the report submission date and compare to the state day count (60 days for a California eFD-1, 30 days for a New York FFA-1, the NAIC OFRS route elsewhere).
Flag any case where the determination date on the file is later than the evidence suggests it should have been, since a late determination hides a late report.
Record on-time percentage by state and hand the late cases to the SIU Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every reportable case has a computed day count against its state deadline and each late report is handed to the SIU Manager.

checklist.step: Assemble the quarterly pack
actions: Build the pack: executive summary, company-level metric table with bands, per-state table for the 51 jurisdictions, outlier list with causes, benchmark comparison and the open remediation log.
Show the movement against the prior quarter and the prior year for every metric so a single-quarter blip is distinguishable from a trend.
Include the data-quality section listing every feed reconciliation break and its status.
Issue the pack by day 20 after quarter end to the Conduct Committee distribution list.
checklist.done: the pack is issued by day 20 with company and per-state tables, banded metrics, causes, benchmarks and the data-quality section.

checklist.step: Run the conduct committee review
actions: Chair the review by day 30 with SIU, Claims, Underwriting, Consumer Affairs and Regulatory Reporting present.
Take each red-band item in turn and require the owning function to state the action, the owner and the date.
Challenge any cause recorded as data quality that has appeared for more than two consecutive quarters.
Record the decisions in the minutes with named owners and dates.
checklist.done: the committee met by day 30 and every red-band item has a minuted action, owner and date.

checklist.step: Raise the red-band items into the issue tracker
actions: Within 5 business days of the committee, raise a GRC issue for each red-band item with the metric, state, value, cause and the minuted action.
Link the issue to the quarterly pack and to the underlying record list so an examiner can follow the chain.
Set the target date from the minutes and the escalation path if the date slips.
Reject any item that arrives without a named individual owner.
checklist.done: every red-band item has a GRC issue with a named owner, target date and links to the pack and record list.

checklist.step: Drive metric-led corrective action into operations
actions: Translate each conduct or referral-rate finding into a specific operational action - a targeted quality-review sweep, a refresher module, or a rule threshold change.
Where the finding is a low referral rate, assign the red-flag refresher module in Cornerstone LMS to the affected state handling teams with a 30-day window.
Where the finding is a denial-rate outlier, launch a focused file review over 30 denied claims in that state and report the results into the next pack.
Confirm each action is closed with evidence rather than with an assertion.
checklist.done: each finding has an operational action with evidence of completion attached, not just an owner.

checklist.step: Track prior-quarter items to closure
actions: Extract all open conduct-metric issues from prior quarters with age, owner and target date.
Verify closure evidence on any item marked complete - a metric that has returned to green for two consecutive quarters, or an implemented configuration change.
Escalate any item over 90 days old or past a second target date to the Head of Compliance.
Carry the open list into the next quarterly pack as a standing section.
checklist.done: every prior item is either closed against evidence, on plan, or escalated with a reason for the slip.

checklist.step: Feed the results into exam readiness and MCAS
actions: Copy the quarterly pack and outlier explanations into the exam readiness file so an examiner question about a ratio has an answer already written.
Cross-check the quarterly claim and complaint metrics against the figures reported in the last MCAS submission and explain any inconsistency.
Update the state risk ranking used to prioritise exam preparation, moving any state with two consecutive red quarters up the list.
Notify Regulatory Reporting of any metric that will look adverse in the next MCAS filing.
checklist.done: the pack is in the exam file, MCAS consistency is checked and the state risk ranking reflects the quarter results.

checklist.step: File and retain the quarterly evidence
actions: File the pack, metric extract, feed reconciliations, benchmark captures, outlier analysis and committee minutes under Conduct Metrics / <quarter>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the quarter-end date.
Index by quarter, state and metric so a single-state history can be produced on request.
Confirm the dataset snapshot behind the pack is retained so the numbers can be reproduced exactly.
checklist.done: the quarterly evidence set including the dataset snapshot is filed, labelled and indexed by quarter, state and metric.

testing.step: Build the population of metrics and states under test
actions: Extract every metric published in the quarter pack at company and state grain, with its value, band and prior-quarter value.
Add every red and amber item raised in the trailing four quarters with its current status.
Confirm the state list covers all 51 jurisdictions and that no state was silently dropped for having no data.
Record the population size and extraction date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population covers every published metric across 51 jurisdictions plus four quarters of open items, with a dated extract.

testing.step: Reconcile the pack figures to the source systems
actions: Re-extract claims opened, closed without payment and denied, SIU cases opened and complaints received for the quarter direct from the source marts.
Compare the totals to the numerators and denominators printed in the pack and compute the variance.
Confirm any prior-quarter figure restated in this pack has a documented cause on the restatement tab.
List every variance above zero on counts for investigation before sampling.
testing.done: pack numerators and denominators reconcile to a re-extraction, with every restatement documented.

testing.step: Draw and document the metric sample
actions: Take 100 percent of red-band metrics and 100 percent of zero-referral states.
Take 12 further state and metric combinations at random using a seeded, reproducible selection.
Ensure the sample includes at least one fraud metric, one timeliness metric and one complaint metric.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes all red bands and zero-referral states, and spans fraud, timeliness and complaint metrics.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled metric from raw records
actions: Read the metric definition sheet formula, then build your own calculation from the raw record extract without reusing the dashboard measure.
Compare your result to the published value and apply the tolerance - exact on counts, 0.1 percentage points on ratios.
Check the state-allocation rule was applied as defined and that the small-population suppression rule did not mask a genuine breach.
Record the recomputation, the published value and the variance in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric has an independent recomputation with a variance inside tolerance or a logged break.

testing.step: Verify the benchmark comparison is genuine
actions: Open the dated benchmark captures filed with the pack and confirm each carries a source, capture date and the peer group used.
Re-retrieve the NAIC complaint index for the company from the Consumer Information Source and compare to the value used in the pack.
Confirm the comparison is like for like on line, period and grain - a company-level index compared to a state-level ratio is an exception.
Capture the re-retrieved benchmark into the workpaper with its date.
testing.done: every benchmark is re-retrievable, dated, like for like, and matches the value used in the pack.

testing.step: Re-perform the bureau-reporting timeliness calculation
actions: Select 20 SIU cases in the quarter that required a state fraud-bureau report and open each case record.
Take the determination date from the investigation narrative rather than the summary field, since a back-dated field hides a late report.
Recompute days to submission against the state day count - 60 days for California, 30 days for New York, and the applicable count elsewhere - and compare to the pack timeliness figure.
Confirm each report has a bureau confirmation reference stored on the case.
testing.done: 20 cases have an independently derived determination date, a recomputed day count and a confirmed bureau reference.

testing.step: Trace red-band items to raised issues and evidenced action
actions: Match every red-band metric in the pack to a GRC issue and check the issue was raised within 5 business days of the committee date.
Open each linked action and confirm the closure evidence is real - a configuration export, a completed training report, a file-review result - not a status update.
Check that any item closed on the basis of the metric returning to green has two consecutive green quarters behind it.
List unraised, late-raised or evidence-free closures as exceptions.
testing.done: every red-band item has a timely issue and evidenced closure, or the gap is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Test the pack production timeliness and distribution
actions: Compare the pack issue date to quarter end plus 20 business days and the committee date to quarter end plus 30.
Confirm the distribution reached the full committee list and that any member absent from the review received the pack and the minutes.
Check the minutes record a decision for each red-band item rather than noting it for discussion.
Log any late pack or committee slippage with the number of days and the stated cause.
testing.done: issue and review dates are measured against the day 20 and day 30 milestones and every slip is logged with a cause.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording quarter, state, metric, published value, recomputed value and the impact on the conclusion drawn.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (definition drift, feed incomplete, suppression rule masked a breach, issue not raised, benchmark stale) and an owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next quarter pack so the fix lands before the next publication.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a pre-next-quarter remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the metric test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the tested metrics and compare it to the recomputation tolerance and the timeliness conditions.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the independent reviewer, who produced no part of the pack, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Conduct Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under Conduct Metrics / <quarter>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
