checklist.step: Structure the exam file against the NAIC exam standards
actions: Create a folder per NAIC Market Regulation Handbook business area - company operations and management, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, and claims - plus a dedicated anti-fraud and SIU folder.
Inside each folder create a standard sub-structure: procedures, evidence samples, system screenshots, data extracts and prior exam findings.
Assign a named section owner and a refresh cadence to every folder and record both on the section register.
Publish the register so every owner can see their sections and next refresh date.
checklist.done: every business area and the anti-fraud section exists with the standard sub-structure, a named owner and a refresh cadence on the register.

checklist.step: Maintain the company profile and organisational evidence
actions: Refresh annually: legal entity chart with NAIC company codes, states of licence and lines written per entity, and the certificate-of-authority register from the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Refresh the org charts for Claims, Underwriting, Compliance and the SIU with reporting lines and headcount as at the refresh date.
List every TPA, MGA and outsourced adjusting firm with its contract reference, states of operation and delegated authority scope.
Record the systems inventory - policy administration, claims, billing, fraud detection - with the version in use and the business owner.
checklist.done: entity, licence, org, delegated-authority and systems evidence are all current within 12 months and dated.

checklist.step: Keep the procedure manual set current and version-controlled
actions: Hold in the file the approved current version of each manual an examiner will ask for: claims handling, underwriting and rating, complaint handling, producer appointment and termination, policyholder service and the anti-fraud plan.
For each manual record the version, approval date, approver and the effective period, and retain the superseded version that was in force during any period likely to fall inside an exam scope.
Confirm the copy in the exam file is byte-identical to the published copy in the document management repository.
Remove drafts and working copies from the folder so nothing unapproved can be produced by accident.
checklist.done: each manual is present at its approved current version with in-force history retained and no drafts in the folder.

checklist.step: Build and prove the standing claims data-call extract
actions: Write the standing claim universe specification to the NAIC exam data request layout: claim number, policy number, state, line, date of loss, date reported, date closed, disposition, paid indemnity, paid expense, denial reason and reopened indicator.
Add the fields an anti-fraud examiner asks for: SIU referral indicator, referral date, disposition and the bureau report reference.
Run the extract quarterly against a rolling 36-month window and record the runtime and row count so the production time is known before an examiner asks.
File the specification, the run log and a sample output in the claims section of the exam file.
checklist.done: the claim universe extract runs to specification on demand with a recorded runtime, row count and sample output on file.

checklist.step: Build and prove the standing underwriting and policy extract
actions: Write the policy universe specification: policy number, state, line, effective and expiration dates, transaction type (new, renewal, cancellation, non-renewal, declination), premium, rating tier, producer code and the reason code for any adverse action.
Include declinations and non-renewals explicitly, since these are the records examiners test for unfair discrimination and notice timing.
Run the extract quarterly over a rolling 36-month window and record the runtime and row count.
File the specification, run log and sample output in the underwriting and rating section.
checklist.done: the policy universe extract including declinations and non-renewals runs to specification with a recorded runtime and sample output.

checklist.step: Maintain the complaint and consumer-contact evidence
actions: Keep the complaint register exam-ready with received date, source (DOI or direct), state, line, complainant, issue code, resolution, resolution date and days to close.
Reconcile the DOI-sourced complaints quarterly to the NAIC Complaints Database records so no state-logged complaint is missing internally.
Retain the full complaint file - correspondence, internal investigation and the response letter - for every DOI complaint, since examiners read the file not the log.
Record the acknowledgement and response day counts against the state prompt-response requirements.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to DOI records quarterly and every DOI complaint has a complete retained file with day counts.

checklist.step: Keep the anti-fraud and SIU section exam-ready
actions: Hold the approved anti-fraud plan, per-state filing confirmations, SIU org chart, investigator credentials and the current FRISS rule and threshold export.
Maintain a quarterly SIU case log by state: cases opened, referral source, disposition, days to disposition, bureau reports filed and the confirmation reference.
Hold a set of 10 exemplar closed case files per major state showing the full trail from red flag to disposition to bureau report.
Keep the anti-fraud training completion extract current so a training question can be answered from the file.
checklist.done: plan, filings, credentials, rule export, case log, exemplar files and training extract are all current within one quarter.

checklist.step: Hold the producer licensing and appointment evidence
actions: Maintain the producer register with NPN, state licences held, appointment dates, termination dates and termination reason codes.
Run the NIPR reconciliation quarterly so every writing producer is licensed and appointed in the state where business was written, and evidence the reconciliation date.
Retain the termination-for-cause notifications filed with each state and the supporting file, since these are read directly in an exam.
Record the commission arrangements and any incentive that an examiner would test against suitability or churning concerns.
checklist.done: the producer register reconciles to NIPR quarterly and every for-cause termination has a retained state notification and file.

checklist.step: Hold the marketing, forms and rating evidence
actions: Keep the approved advertising inventory with piece id, media, states used, approval date and approver, plus the withdrawn-piece list.
Hold the SERFF tracking numbers and approval letters for the forms and rates currently in use per state so filed-versus-used can be evidenced immediately.
Hold the current rating manual, rate pages and the effective dates in force in each state.
Cross-check the rating configuration in production against the filed rate pages for the three highest-premium states each quarter.
checklist.done: advertising, form and rate evidence is current with SERFF references and a quarterly filed-versus-used cross-check for the top three states.

checklist.step: Track the state exam pipeline and pre-exam signals
actions: Maintain the exam register: state, exam type, period examined, examiner-in-charge, dates and status for every exam in the last 7 years.
Monitor pre-exam signals - market analysis questionnaires, complaint index movement, MCAS ratio outliers and information requests - and log each with a date.
Rank states by exam likelihood using time since last exam, complaint index and MCAS outlier count, and refresh the ranking quarterly.
Brief the Head of Compliance whenever a state moves into the top five so the relevant sections get an early refresh.
checklist.done: the exam register is complete for 7 years, pre-exam signals are logged and the state ranking is refreshed quarterly.

checklist.step: Rehearse the first 72 hours of an exam notice
actions: Maintain the exam runbook: who receives the notice, who is named exam coordinator, how the examiner data call is logged and the 10 business day clock started.
Name the section liaisons for claims, underwriting, complaints, producer and SIU and confirm each has a deputy.
State the single-channel rule - all documents leave through the exam coordinator, after Regulatory Counsel privilege review - and the rule against direct examiner contact by operating staff.
Rehearse the runbook annually with the named liaisons and record the attendance.
checklist.done: the runbook names the coordinator, liaisons and deputies, states the single-channel and privilege rules, and was rehearsed within 12 months.

checklist.step: Run an unannounced mock data call each half year
actions: Draft a mock data call modelled on a real NAIC exam request - claim universe for two states over 24 months, 25 named claim files, the anti-fraud plan and the SIU case log.
Issue it without warning to the exam coordinator and start the 10 business day clock.
Measure elapsed days to a complete, counsel-cleared production and record what had to be built rather than pulled.
Write the gap list from the exercise into the section register as dated remediation items.
checklist.done: a mock data call was run in the half year, timed against 10 business days, with a dated gap list on the register.

checklist.step: Refresh sections on cadence and evidence the refresh
actions: Ten business days before each section refresh date, notify the named owner with the specific artefacts due.
On receipt, replace the artefact, stamp the refresh date and the owner name in the section register, and archive the superseded version rather than deleting it.
Escalate any section 10 business days past its refresh date to the Head of Compliance with the owner named.
Report the file staleness position - sections current, due, overdue - into the quarterly conduct pack.
checklist.done: every section shows a stamped refresh date and owner, with overdue sections escalated and reported in the quarterly pack.

checklist.step: Keep prior exam findings and their status inside the file
actions: Hold every exam report from the last 7 years with the findings list, the agreed corrective actions and the current closure status of each.
Attach the closure evidence to each finding so a follow-up examiner can verify without a new request.
Flag any finding closed on assertion rather than evidence and reopen it.
Include any regulatory settlement agreement, consent order and fine with its payment and compliance-condition status.
checklist.done: every prior finding carries its corrective action, closure evidence and current status, with settlements and their conditions included.

checklist.step: Control access, privilege and retention on the file
actions: Restrict edit access to named section owners and read access to Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit, and review the access list quarterly.
Mark counsel-prepared analyses as privileged and store them in a separate sub-folder that is never included in a production set by default.
Apply the 7-year-from-exam-close retention label and confirm no section is on a shorter default policy.
Confirm the file is indexed by state, exam year and exam standard so a request can be met without a manual sweep.
checklist.done: access is restricted and quarterly reviewed, privileged material is segregated, and the whole file carries the 7-year label and the required indexing.

testing.step: Build the population of exam-file sections and data calls
actions: Extract the section register with every section, named owner, refresh cadence, last refresh date and artefact list.
Add every examiner or state data call received in the last 12 months with its receipt date and response date.
Add every standing extract specification with its last successful run date and row count.
Confirm the section list covers all seven NAIC business areas plus the anti-fraud section, and record the population size and date.
testing.done: the population covers all business areas, standing extracts and 12 months of data calls, with a dated extract.

testing.step: Reconcile the file contents to the register
actions: Walk the repository folder tree and confirm every artefact the register claims is actually present and openable.
Confirm every manual in the file is byte-identical to the published version in the document management repository and is the approved version, not a draft.
List register entries with no artefact, and artefacts sitting outside the register, as automatic exceptions.
Compute the staleness position - sections current, due, overdue - directly from the file dates rather than the register field.
testing.done: every register entry reconciles to a present, approved artefact and the staleness position is derived from file dates.

testing.step: Draw and document the section and file sample
actions: Take 100 percent of the anti-fraud and SIU section and 100 percent of sections flagged overdue.
Take 8 further sections at random using a seeded, reproducible selection across the business areas.
Within the claims and underwriting sections, select 25 claim files and 25 policy transactions at random from the standing universe extracts.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes the anti-fraud section and all overdue sections, and carries 25 claim and 25 policy records.

testing.step: Re-run the standing extracts and time them
actions: Ask the Data Analyst to execute the claim universe and policy universe extracts live in your presence against a two-state, 24-month scope.
Time the run end to end and compare the row counts to the operational reports for the same scope.
Check every field in the specification actually populates - a blank SIU referral or denial reason column is a readiness failure, not a data nuance.
Capture the run log, timings and a redacted sample into the workpaper.
testing.done: both universes ran live, reconciled on row count, populated every specified field, and the timings are recorded.

testing.step: Trace sampled claim and policy records to complete files
actions: For each of the 25 sampled claims, open the file and confirm the documents an examiner reads are present: first notice, coverage analysis, adjuster notes, reserve history, correspondence, payment or denial letter and any SIU referral record.
For each of the 25 sampled policy transactions, confirm the application, rating worksheet, issued documents and any adverse-action notice with its mailing date are retrievable.
Measure retrieval time per file and flag anything that required an out-of-system request.
Log any file with a missing mandatory document as an exception naming the document.
testing.done: each sampled claim and policy file is retrievable with its mandatory documents present, and retrieval times are recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the anti-fraud section readiness check
actions: Confirm the anti-fraud plan version in the exam file equals the approved and filed version, and that per-state filing confirmations are attached.
Compare the FRISS rule and threshold export in the file to a live export taken on the test date and log any drift.
Open 5 of the exemplar closed SIU case files and confirm each shows red flag, investigation steps, disposition and a bureau report reference where required.
Confirm the training completion extract in the file is no more than one quarter old.
testing.done: plan version, filings, live rule export, exemplar case trails and training extract all reconcile as at the test date.

testing.step: Recompute data-call response timing against the 10-day standard
actions: For every data call in the last 12 months, take the receipt date from the incoming correspondence rather than the internal log.
Compute business days to the complete, counsel-cleared production and compare to the 10 business day standard.
Where a production was made in tranches, measure to the final tranche, since a partial response does not stop the clock.
Include the mock data call in the same calculation and note whether the file or a build supplied the answer.
testing.done: every data call including the mock has a recomputed business-day count measured to the final tranche.

testing.step: Test access control, privilege segregation and retention
actions: Export the access list for the exam file and compare it to the approved owner and reader list, checking for leavers and role changes.
Confirm the privileged sub-folder is excluded from the default production set by attempting a mock production and inspecting what is included.
Confirm the 7-year-from-exam-close retention label is applied at folder level and that no sub-folder inherits a shorter default.
Log any leaver with retained access or any privileged document reachable in a default production as a control exception.
testing.done: access matches the approved list, privileged material stays out of a default production, and the retention label holds throughout.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception recording the section, the missing or stale artefact and the exam risk it creates.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (owner vacancy, cadence not enforced, extract broken by a system change, document not published, access drift) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current refresh cycle and, for a broken standing extract, treat it as high priority since it drives the 10 day standard.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, an in-cycle remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the readiness test
actions: Compute the section exception rate and compare it to the 5 percent threshold and the zero-tolerance conditions on ownerless sections and late data calls.
State separately whether the mock data call met the 10 business day standard, since that is the operative readiness measure.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it and have the independent reviewer, who owns no tested section, sign it.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under Exam Readiness / <period>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the exception rate, the mock data-call result and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the remediation of every market conduct exam finding end to end; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the examiner relationship and the SIU Manager owns any anti-fraud or SIU finding

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the state exam authority statute and the corrective-action or settlement terms in the adopted report for each exam, read with the underlying substantive requirement, including the Alaska anti-fraud plan / SIU requirement and the Arizona, California and Connecticut SIU requirements where a finding touches fraud controls

In-scope processes.value: Draft exam report review and rebuttal, root cause analysis, corrective action plan design, process and system change, consumer restitution, re-training, closure evidence and the regulator confirmation, for every open finding across all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Findings, actions, evidence and closure sign-offs tracked in the GRC platform, with restitution executed through the Claims Platform or billing/commission platform and the audit trail retained in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure - draft report triage, rebuttal drafting and the state response window, root cause taxonomy, corrective action plan template, restitution calculation and payment standards, closure evidence standards and independent validation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel clearance on the rebuttal and settlement sections, reviewed annually and after any exam that produced a settlement agreement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven from the exam - typically a 30 day window to respond to the draft report before adoption, the corrective action dates fixed in the adopted report or regulatory settlement agreement (commonly 30/60/90 days), any fine payment date, and the state follow-up or re-exam date

Deadline reminders configured.value: On logging a draft report the GRC platform opens a 30 day rebuttal clock with reminders at day 10 and day 20; each corrective action carries reminders at T-30, T-14 and T-3 to its committed date, and a breach alert to the Head of Compliance on the day it passes

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and adopted reports, the rebuttal, the corrective action plan, root cause analyses, restitution registers with payment proof, re-training records, validation workpapers and the regulator closure letter retained 7 years from exam close, indexed by state and exam year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed rebuttal window, a corrective action past its committed date, restitution unpaid or returned undelivered, and any finding closed without independent validation is logged as an exception with root cause, owner and a new date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the closure of every finding after independent validation, and personally approves any request to the state to extend a committed corrective-action date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every market conduct exam finding open or closed in the last 24 months across all states, together with the restitution population attached to each finding and every extension request made

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missed rebuttal window, a corrective action closed after its committed date without an agreed extension, and a finding closed without independent validation evidence; restitution must reconcile to the affected-population calculation exactly, with any shortfall a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; each finding is validated individually before closure and the whole open population is tested quarterly, with a full 24-month look-back test annually

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance and the remediating business function and must not have performed or approved any tested corrective action

Evidence location for test results.value: Exam remediation test workpaper (finding inventory, date recomputation, restitution reconciliation, sampled closure evidence re-performance, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Exam Remediation / <state> / <exam year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Finding-by-finding status pack with corrective action, evidence reference, completion date, restitution totals and the validation sign-off, producible for a follow-up inquiry or re-exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The exam coordinator in Market Conduct Compliance is the only channel to the examiner-in-charge and the state; Regulatory Counsel drafts or clears the rebuttal, any extension request and any communication that concedes a violation

checklist.step: Log the draft exam report and start the response clock
actions: Register the draft report in the GRC platform on the day of receipt with state, exam period, examiner-in-charge, receipt date and the stated response due date.
Confirm the response window from the transmittal letter - most states allow 30 days from the draft report date - and open the clock with day 10 and day 20 reminders.
Split the report into individual findings, one GRC record each, with the exam standard, criteria, condition, error rate cited and the recommendation.
Distribute each finding to the owning function head and to Regulatory Counsel the same week.
checklist.done: the draft report is registered with a running clock and every finding exists as a separate record with a named owning function.

checklist.step: Verify the examiner error rate against the underlying records
actions: Obtain the examiner sample list and the exception schedule behind each finding.
Pull each cited claim, policy or complaint record and re-read it to determine whether the cited condition is present.
Compute your own error rate over the examiner sample and compare it to the rate in the finding.
Where the examiner miscounted or misread a record, prepare the evidence pack showing the specific record and the correct facts - never dispute a finding on argument alone.
checklist.done: each finding has a re-computed error rate and a record-level evidence pack supporting agreement or dispute.

checklist.step: Draft the rebuttal and file it inside the response window
actions: For each finding state one of: agree, agree in part with clarification, or disagree with the evidentiary basis.
Reference the specific record and document for every disagreement and attach the evidence pack.
Where the finding is agreed, state the corrective action and the date rather than leaving the state to impose one.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the response and send it through the exam coordinator before the day-30 deadline, retaining the transmission proof.
checklist.done: the response is sent through the exam coordinator before the window closes with transmission proof retained, and every finding has a stated position.

checklist.step: Perform root cause analysis on every agreed finding
actions: Run a structured analysis per finding - five whys or fishbone - with the operating team present, not from the compliance desk.
Classify the cause: procedure gap, system configuration, training gap, staffing or workload, vendor performance, or data quality.
Test the cause against the population - if the cause is real, the same defect should be visible in records the examiner never sampled.
Write the cause statement onto the GRC finding record with the population evidence supporting it.
checklist.done: each finding has a classified root cause validated against records outside the examiner sample.

checklist.step: Size the affected population beyond the examiner sample
actions: Build the full population that could carry the same defect across the exam period and, where the defect persisted, up to the present date.
Extend the query to every state with the same procedure or configuration, since a defect found in one state rarely stops at the border.
Quantify the exposure: number of records affected, dollars involved and the consumer impact per record.
Deliver the population file with the query, run date and row count so the restitution calculation can be reproduced.
checklist.done: a reproducible affected-population file exists covering all states and periods carrying the same defect, with quantified exposure.

checklist.step: Write the corrective action plan with dates and owners
actions: For each finding record the immediate containment action, the permanent fix, the restitution action where consumers were harmed, and the monitoring that proves it stays fixed.
Set each action against the date fixed in the adopted report or settlement agreement - commonly 30, 60 or 90 days - and never a date later than the committed one.
Name an individual owner and an executive sponsor for each action, and record the evidence that will prove completion before work begins.
Have the owning function head accept the plan in writing in the GRC record.
checklist.done: every finding has containment, permanent fix, restitution and monitoring actions with individual owners, committed dates and pre-agreed closure evidence.

checklist.step: Implement the procedure and system changes
actions: Raise the change request for each system fix with the finding reference in the title so the audit trail is unambiguous.
Where the fix is a validation or a mandatory field - for example a required SIU referral reason or a denial reason code - build it as an enforced control rather than guidance.
Update the affected procedure document, version it and route it for approval through the normal document control route.
Confirm the change reached production with a post-implementation check on live records, not on the test environment.
checklist.done: each system fix is live and verified on production records, and each procedure change is versioned and approved.

checklist.step: Calculate and execute consumer restitution
actions: Compute the amount due per affected consumer using the method the state accepted, including interest at the state statutory rate from the original due date where required.
Build the restitution register: consumer, policy or claim number, state, original amount, interest, total due, payment date, payment reference and delivery status.
Issue payments with an explanatory letter cleared by Regulatory Counsel, and track returned or undeliverable payments to an escheatment or re-search process rather than closing them.
Reconcile the register total to the general ledger postings and to the affected-population file before reporting completion.
checklist.done: every affected consumer has a computed amount, an issued payment with a tracked delivery status, and the register reconciles to the population file and the ledger.

checklist.step: Retrain the affected population and evidence it
actions: Build the targeted module from the actual finding, using redacted examples of the defective records so the lesson is concrete.
Assign it in Cornerstone LMS to the specific handling teams and states named in the finding with a 30 day completion window.
Include a knowledge check and set a pass mark so completion means comprehension rather than attendance.
Deliver the completion and pass-rate extract to the Compliance Officer as the closure evidence for the training action.
checklist.done: the targeted module is assigned, completed inside 30 days with a recorded pass rate, and the extract is filed as closure evidence.

checklist.step: Stand up the monitoring that proves the fix holds
actions: Define the metric that would move if the defect recurred - the same measure the examiner used where possible - and add it to the quarterly conduct pack.
Set the alert threshold at the level the finding would have triggered and name the recipient.
Run a post-fix quality review over 30 records processed after the change and confirm the defect rate is zero.
Record both the metric definition and the post-fix review result on the GRC finding record.
checklist.done: a named metric with an alert threshold is live in the quarterly pack and a 30-record post-fix review shows a zero defect rate.

checklist.step: Assemble the closure evidence pack per finding
actions: Collect for each finding: root cause statement, affected population file, change request and production verification, updated procedure version, restitution register with payment proof, training extract and post-fix review.
Check every item against the closure evidence agreed when the plan was written - substituted evidence is not accepted.
File the pack under Exam Remediation / <state> / <exam year> / <finding id>.
Mark the GRC record ready for validation only when the pack is complete.
checklist.done: each finding has a complete evidence pack matching the pre-agreed evidence standard and is marked ready for validation.

checklist.step: Obtain independent validation before closing
actions: Take each ready-for-validation finding and re-perform the key evidence rather than reading the summary.
Re-run the affected-population query yourself and confirm the restitution register covers it with no residual population.
Test 10 post-change records for the defect and confirm the enforced control cannot be bypassed.
Record a validation conclusion of validated or returned, with the specific reason where returned, on the GRC record.
checklist.done: each finding carries a documented validation conclusion based on re-performed evidence, not a review of the summary.

checklist.step: Close the finding and confirm status to the state
actions: Review the validation conclusion and sign the closure on the GRC record with the date.
Produce the finding-by-finding status pack for the state showing action, evidence reference, completion date and restitution total.
Send it through the exam coordinator by the date the adopted report or settlement agreement requires, and log the transmission.
Where a date cannot be met, have Regulatory Counsel request an extension in writing before the date passes - never after.
checklist.done: each finding is signed closed against validation and the state has received the status pack by its required date, with any extension requested in advance.

checklist.step: Roll the fix across the other jurisdictions
actions: For each finding, decide explicitly whether the same defect exists in the other 50 jurisdictions and record the decision with its basis.
Where it does, open a self-identified remediation item with the same corrective action, population sizing and restitution standard.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether any state requires a self-report of the self-identified issue and record the decision.
Report the multi-state rollout status into the quarterly conduct pack until every jurisdiction is closed.
checklist.done: every finding carries a recorded multi-state applicability decision and each applicable jurisdiction has an opened, tracked remediation item.

checklist.step: Retain the remediation record and feed it back into the exam file
actions: File the draft and adopted reports, rebuttal, plan, evidence packs, restitution registers, validation workpapers and the regulator closure letter under Exam Remediation / <state> / <exam year>.
Apply the 7-year-from-exam-close retention label and index by state, exam year and finding id.
Copy the finding status pack into the exam readiness file so a follow-up examiner sees closure evidence without a new data call.
Confirm the restitution register is retained with its payment proof, since it is the item examiners return to most often.
checklist.done: the full remediation record is filed with a 7-year label, indexed by finding, and the status pack is mirrored into the exam readiness file.

testing.step: Build the population of findings and committed dates
actions: Extract every market conduct exam finding open or closed in the last 24 months with state, exam year, finding id, owner, committed date, status and closure date.
Add every restitution register and every extension request attached to those findings.
Reconcile the finding count to the adopted exam reports themselves, counting findings in the reports rather than trusting the tracker.
Record the population size, source and extraction date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled directly to the adopted exam reports, with restitution registers and extensions attached.

testing.step: Reconcile the tracker to the adopted report language
actions: Read each adopted report and compare its findings and required corrective actions to the wording in the GRC records.
Flag any finding narrowed in the tracker relative to the report, and any required action that never became a tracked action.
Confirm every fine or settlement condition in the report has a corresponding tracked item with a payment or compliance date.
List all differences as automatic exceptions before sampling.
testing.done: every report finding, required action and settlement condition is matched to a tracked item, or the gap is listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the finding sample
actions: Take 100 percent of findings with consumer restitution, 100 percent of findings touching the anti-fraud plan or SIU, and 100 percent of findings closed after their committed date.
Take 10 further findings at random using a seeded, reproducible selection from the remainder.
Within each restitution finding, sample 25 payments for tracing.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers all restitution, anti-fraud and late-closed findings plus a reproducible random selection, with 25 payments per restitution finding.

testing.step: Re-perform the root cause and population sizing
actions: Re-run the affected-population query for each sampled finding using your own filters derived from the finding wording, not the analyst script.
Compare your population count to the one used for remediation and investigate any shortfall, since an undersized population understates restitution.
Test whether the population was extended to every state and period carrying the same procedure or configuration.
Capture your query, run date and counts into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independently derived affected population compared to the one remediated, with any shortfall quantified.

testing.step: Verify the fix is enforced in production
actions: For each sampled system fix, open the production configuration and confirm the control is enforced rather than advisory.
Attempt the defective path on a test transaction in the production-mirrored environment and confirm the system blocks it.
Trace the change back to the change request carrying the finding reference and confirm the deployment date pre-dates the closure date.
Log any fix that is guidance-only, deployed after closure, or absent from production as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled fix is proven enforced in production with a deployment date earlier than the finding closure date.

testing.step: Trace restitution payments to proof of delivery
actions: For the 25 sampled payments per finding, trace each register row to a payment record with amount, date and reference in the disbursement system.
Recompute the amount due including statutory interest from the original due date and compare to the amount paid.
Check the treatment of returned or undeliverable payments - confirm a re-search or escheatment step exists rather than a silent write-off.
Reconcile the register total to the general ledger posting and to the affected-population count.
testing.done: sampled payments trace to disbursement records with recomputed amounts and interest, and the register reconciles to the ledger and population.

testing.step: Recompute every deadline in the remediation chain
actions: Recompute the draft report response due date from the transmittal letter date plus the state window - typically 30 days - and compare to the send date on the transmission proof.
Recompute each corrective action due date from the adopted report or settlement agreement and compare to the actual completion date.
For every extension, confirm the request was made and granted before the original date passed, not after.
Treat any action closed after its committed date without a pre-agreed extension as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every response, action and extension date is recomputed from source documents with an on-time or late conclusion recorded.

testing.step: Test the independence and sufficiency of the closure validation
actions: Confirm each sampled finding carries a validation conclusion from someone outside the remediating function and outside Compliance.
Compare the evidence relied on at validation to the closure evidence agreed when the plan was written, and flag every substitution.
Re-test 10 post-change records yourself for two sampled findings and confirm the defect rate is zero.
Confirm the Head of Compliance closure signature post-dates the validation conclusion.
testing.done: every sampled closure has independent validation on the pre-agreed evidence, a zero post-change defect rate and a correctly sequenced sign-off.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with state, exam year, finding id, what failed and the regulatory exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (population undersized, fix advisory only, restitution incomplete, date missed, validation not independent, multi-state rollout skipped) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a committed regulatory date was missed or restitution was short, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel before contacting the state.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly remediation test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the remediation test
actions: Compute the exception rate over tested findings and state separately whether any zero-tolerance condition was breached - missed rebuttal window, late closure without extension, or closure without independent validation.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed and approved none of the tested corrective actions, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and, where a settlement condition is at risk, to the Board Risk Committee, then file the workpaper under Exam Remediation / <state> / <exam year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the exception rate, any zero-tolerance breach and the committee reporting date.
